design.item: First open / re-index bulk load (file graphs): defer SQLite stores across files with a flush budget based on measured cost, a batch reset-files API that yields, no per-file root re-render, crash-consistent checkpoints and a recovery route
design.summary:
Worktree: /home/johan/dev/logsidian-perf. The fork's DataScript `-transact!` strips `:skip-store?` (conn.cljc:104) before `store-after-transact!` reads it (conn.cljc:90). A caller can only defer a store by doing `d/with` and then `store-after-transact!` itself with the flag in the report. The DB-graph branch of `ldb/transact-sync` does exactly that (db.cljs:110-128); file graphs fall through to `d/transact!` (db.cljs:138), so every file stores. Nothing in the app ever flushes a deferred tail. The design has six steps.

Step 0: measure store bytes per index class (EAVT, AEVT, AVET, branch, root, tail) and per attribute inside the SQLite `-store`.

Step 1: add a guarded `:bulk-load?` branch in `transact-sync`. It appends to `:tx-tail` without writing. A new `flush-deferred-store!` does one forced `store-impl!`: one `-store` call, so one SQLite transaction. The worker flushes when the pending tail passes a datom budget, and the budget adapts to each flush's measured time (target 150 ms). This bounds every flush by cost, so it stays bounded even under AVET `:block/title` amplification. In the worst case it degrades to today's per-file granularity, never worse.

Step 2: a new `:thread-api/reset-files` takes about 64 files (or 512 KB) per call. It runs files in order, each as its own DataScript tx, and yields through a MessageChannel every ~50 ms. Calls are chained per repo. Each file returns only `{:path :page-name | :error}`, never the whole tx. The UI loop sends chunks instead of one file per round trip.

Step 3: the UI pipeline skips `re-render-root!` for `:bulk-load?` syncs. The single final re-render goes through `pub-event! [:ui/re-render-root]`, so it queues behind every `:db/sync-changes` already posted.

Step 4 (crash): SQLite always holds the db as of the last flush, which is a prefix of whole files. The next open already re-parses the missing files through `load-graph-files!`, but on the slow per-file path and without `:graph/added`. The design routes more than 100 missing files through the same bulk loader.

The AVET `:block/title` index (file schema:79, full block text sorted by value) limits how far Step 1 can amortize. The fuller version drops that index for new file graphs. The only readers on file graphs are one full scan (`reference.cljs:133`) and DB-only lookups, but the fork raises on AVET access to a non-indexed attribute, so the readers must switch first. Also optional: stop mirroring bulk txs to the UI at all and reload initial data at the end.
design.current_behavior:
WHERE DEFERRAL EXISTS AND WHY FILE GRAPHS DON'T GET IT
- Fork = ~/.gitlibs/libs/datascript/datascript/3971e2d43bd93d89f42191dc7b4b092989e0cc61/src/datascript.
- `store-after-transact!` (conn.cljc:82-99):
  - always conj's the tx datoms onto the conn's `:tx-tail` (conn.cljc:89)
  - skips storing only if the report's `[:tx-meta :skip-store?]` is set (conn.cljc:90)
  - if the tail passes the branching factor, calls `storage/store-impl!` and resets the tail (conn.cljc:91-97); otherwise `store-tail` rewrites the whole tail as one row (conn.cljc:99, storage.cljs:141-142).
- `-transact!` does `(dissoc tx-meta :skip-store?)` before `with` (conn.cljc:104), so through `d/transact!` the flag never reaches the report.
- The worker's `:thread-api/transact` adds `:skip-store? true` ("delay writes to the disk", db_worker.cljs:618-621).
- `ldb/transact!` → `transact-sync` (deps/db/src/logseq/db.cljs:105; dispatch at 177-179).
  - DB graphs: `d/with` keeps tx-meta; the branch then calls `reset! conn` (126), `dc/store-after-transact!` (127) and `dc/run-callbacks` (128), so the flag is honoured.
  - File graphs: plain `(d/transact! conn tx-data tx-meta)` (138), which stores every transact.
- No flush exists anywhere: grep finds no `store-impl!`, `storage/store` or `:tx-tail` in src/ or deps/.
  - A deferred tail is written only by the next non-skip transact.
  - close-db-aux! only closes the handles (db_worker.cljs:266-277).
  - In DB graphs the listener's own follow-up transact (db_listener.cljs:53-68, `:skip-validate-db?` → `d/transact!`) is what usually flushes.

WHAT A STORE WRITES
- `store-impl!` (storage.cljs:91-124):
  - calls `set/store` on eavt/aevt/avet
  - then the root meta (addr 0) and an empty tail (addr 1), in ONE `-store` call (116-123)
  - that is ONE SQLite `.transaction` (upsert-addr-content!, db_worker.cljs:148-157), which upserts in place (`on conflict(addr) do update`, 156).
- persistent-sorted-set 0.1.2 (~/.m2/.../persistent-sorted-set-0.1.2.jar, persistent_sorted_set.cljs):
  - It writes only nodes that are dirty or have no address (Leaf store-aux 510-516; Node 377-392, recursing into dirty children at 383).
  - Modified nodes keep their old `_address` and are created dirty (new-node 347-358, new-leaf 500-506). Correction to the prior design: dirtiness, not a missing address, is what makes a node need a write.
  - Dirty children stay strongly referenced. Only after a store does set-address! wrap them in a WeakRef (340-345). A later read restores an evicted child from SQLite (node-child 429-445).
  - StorageAdapter.store reuses the node's address and generates a new one only for new or split nodes (storage.cljs:42-48).
- Leaves are capped by entry count (512), not bytes. Text-bearing leaves:
  - AEVT `:file/content` run: ~4 KB per file, appended at the end of the run
  - AEVT/EAVT `:block/title`
  - AVET `:block/title`: `:db/index true`, file_based/schema.cljs:79; blocks keep their full text there; sorted by value, so new blocks land scattered
  - refs are AVET-indexed automatically (fork db.cljc:877, `:db.type/ref [:db.type/ref :db/index]`).
- The 10k SQLite db is 98 MB (prof-10k-after OPFS file) for 41 MB of markdown.

MEASURED
From ~/.cache/lsbench/after/open-10k/open-console.log, 3852 reset-file records:

| per file | median | mean | p90 | p99 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| store-ms | 50 | 52 | 89 | 228 | 989 |
| worker total | 89 | 103 | 196 | — | — |
| transact beyond store | 18 | 25.6 | — | — | — |
| extract | 13 | 17 | — | — | — |
| mldoc | 4 | 7.6 | — | — | — |

- store-calls is always 1 per file.
- store-ms is bimodal: 24 % of files are under 10 ms (the tail-only store-tail branch); the rest 30-200+ ms (store-impl!).
- The store median rises 47 → 52 ms over 4000 files.
- Restores during parse: median 44 per 1 s window, ~20 ms restoring, rising from 4 to 25 ms over the run.

PARSE LOOP
- The UI go-loop is repo.cljs:155-215, one file in flight (179-214).
- Each file goes parse-and-load-file! (91-114) → alter-file (file.cljs:139-193):
  - builds a fixed opts map (154-158)
  - retracts alias/tags when the page exists (161-165)
  - calls reset-file! (36-40) → `:thread-api/reset-file` (db_worker.cljs:843-870) → file-reset/reset-file! (reset.cljs:99-116, returns the whole tx) → graph-parser/parse-file, which transacts with `(select-keys options [:new-graph? :from-disk?])` (graph_parser.cljs:194).
- The whole tx is transit-written back to the UI, only so the loop can find the page name (repo.cljs:195-199).
- Every tx is also broadcast: db_listener.cljs:19-44 → shared_service.cljs:359-366, posted on the worker port and on the common channel. The worker's invoke-hooks returns only `{:tx-report}` for from-disk txs (worker/pipeline.cljs:512-518), and FTS is skipped for them (db_listener.cljs:36).
- On the UI: handler/worker.cljs:45-46 re-publishes the sync via pub-event! → events go-loop (events.cljs:432-451) → :db/sync-changes (406-412) → pipeline invoke-hooks. For from-disk txs that branch transacts into the UI conn and calls `re-render-root!` on every file (modules/outliner/pipeline.cljs:56-59).
- End of loop: after-parse (repo.cljs:141-152) re-renders once directly (145-146) and pubs `:graph/added` (147 → events.cljs:70-76: search rebuild, redirect home, watch-dir!).

CRASH / NEXT OPEN
- native_fs.cljs:130-142 runs add-repo! and <export-db without waiting for the parse, because load-new-repo-to-db! returns a core.async channel (repo.cljs:215) that p/do! treats as a plain value. So the graph is in the repo list from the start.
- Next launch: handler.cljs:69-73 restore-graph! → :graph/restored (restore.cljs:38) → :graph/ready (events.cljs:260-265) → load-graph-files! (events.cljs:188).
- load-graph-files! (watcher_handler.cljs:136-206):
  - reads all db paths (143) and the directory
  - issues, concurrently for every file (p/all, 186-197), fs/read-file plus handle-changed!, which fetches the db content per file (77).
  - A missing file is an "add" with content ≠ "" → handle-add-and-change! → alter-file `{:re-render-root? true :from-disk? true}` (57-61): the non-bulk per-file store plus two re-renders.
  - :graph/added is never pubbed on this path.

Listeners see `:bulk-load?`, never `:skip-store?`.

(defn deferred-datoms [conn] (transduce (map count) + 0 (:tx-tail @(:atom conn))))

(defn flush-deferred-store!
  "Write all dirty index nodes + root + empty tail in ONE IStorage -store call
   (one SQLite transaction). Returns ms spent, nil when nothing is pending."
  [conn]
  (let [db @conn]
    (when-let [adapter (storage/storage-adapter db)]
      (when (seq (:tx-tail @(:atom conn)))
        (let [t0 (js/performance.now)]
          (storage/store-impl! db adapter true)
          (swap! (:atom conn) assoc :tx-tail [] :db-last-stored db)
          (- (js/performance.now) t0))))))

Notes:
- This is the overflow branch of store-after-transact! (conn.cljc:91-97), forced.
- `force? true` always writes the root and an empty tail.
- `(:atom conn)` is reached exactly as conn.cljc:88 does.
- Why count the tail instead of keeping a separate counter: any unplanned checkpoint by a non-bulk transact (tail overflow → store-impl!, which resets the tail) keeps the count right automatically.
- If the non-bulk transact writes only the tail (store-tail), root plus replayed tail is still a consistent pair: restore-impl replays it (storage.cljs:144-170).
- Leave `:thread-api/transact`'s `:skip-store?` (db_worker.cljs:618-621) as it is. It stays a no-op for file graphs; honouring it would need an idle flush policy, which is out of scope.

changes.change:
STEP 1b: a flush budget based on measured cost. This answers the critique's required change 2.

(def ^:private bulk-target-ms 150)
(def ^:private bulk-min-datoms 512)     ; = the tail threshold store-after-transact! uses today, i.e. today's per-file granularity
(def ^:private bulk-max-datoms 65536)   ; caps pinned dirty nodes + tail memory
(def ^:private bulk-initial-datoms 1024)
(defonce ^:private *bulk-budget (atom {})) ; repo -> datoms
(defn next-bulk-budget [budget ms]      ; pure, unit-tested
  (-> (* budget (-> (js/Math.sqrt (/ bulk-target-ms (max ms 1))) (max 0.5) (min 2)))
      js/Math.round (max bulk-min-datoms) (min bulk-max-datoms)))
(defn- bulk-maybe-flush! [repo conn force?]
  (let [n (ldb/deferred-datoms conn) budget (get @*bulk-budget repo bulk-initial-datoms)]
    (when (and (pos? n) (or force? (>= n budget)))
      (when-let [ms (ldb/flush-deferred-store! conn)]
        (when-not force? (swap! *bulk-budget assoc repo (next-bulk-budget budget ms)))
        (perf-log! "bulk-flush" {:datoms n :ms (js/Math.round ms) :budget budget :forced force? ...step-0 bytes-by-class})))))

Why this controller:
- A flush costs about a + c·(dirty bytes).
- The append-only parts amortize, so the budget grows until a flush costs ~150 ms.
- If AVET title saturation makes the flush cost grow with the graph, the budget shrinks toward 512 datoms, i.e. today's behaviour. The stall stays bounded and per-file cost is never worse than today.

STEP 2a, batch API:

(defonce ^:private *bulk-chain (atom {}))
(defn- yield! [] (js/Promise. (fn [res] (let [ch (js/MessageChannel.)] (set! (.. ch -port1 -onmessage) (fn [_] (res nil))) (.postMessage (.-port2 ch) nil)))))
(def-thread-api :thread-api/reset-files
  [repo files opts]  ; files: [{:file/path :file/content :stat {:ctime :mtime}}], opts {:new-graph?}
  (let [run (fn [] (when-let [conn (worker-state/get-datascript-conn repo)]
              (p/loop [fs (seq files) acc [] t (js/performance.now)]
                (if-let [f (first fs)]
                  (let [r (file-reset/bulk-reset-file! repo conn f opts)]   ; sync, per-file try/catch
                    (bulk-maybe-flush! repo conn false)
                    (if (> (- (js/performance.now) t) 50)
                      (p/let [_ (yield!)] (p/recur (next fs) (conj acc r) (js/performance.now)))
                      (p/recur (next fs) (conj acc r) t)))
                  acc))))
        p' (p/then (get @*bulk-chain repo (p/resolved nil)) (fn [_] (run)))]
    (swap! *bulk-chain assoc repo (p/catch p' (constantly nil)))
    (arm-idle-flush! repo)  ; 2 s timer: (bulk-maybe-flush! repo conn true) if no further call arrives
    p'))

(def-thread-api :thread-api/flush-storage [repo]
  (when-let [conn (worker-state/get-datascript-conn repo)] (bulk-maybe-flush! repo conn true))
  nil)
It MUST return nil. store-impl! returns the db, which would otherwise be transit-serialized.

How the batch API behaves:
- MessageChannel, not setTimeout 0: nested timeouts clamp to 4 ms.
- Queued Comlink messages (queries, other transacts) run between files, and each sees a db that is consistent per file.
- The per-repo chain keeps files in UI order even if the UI pipelines two calls.
- remote-function already awaits promise results (thread_api.cljc p/let on result-promise). Its perf `sync-ms` will then show only the first slice.
- Refactor the LSPERF per-file timing code of :thread-api/reset-file (847-869) into one fn and use it from bulk-reset-file! too, so the harness keeps its per-file records.
- close-db-aux! (266): before the dissoc's, `(when-let [conn (get @*datascript-conns repo)] (ldb/flush-deferred-store! conn))`, so a graph switch during a load persists what is pending. The work is bounded by the budget.

ORDERING
- The final re-render and `:graph/added` go through pub-event!, so they queue behind every `:db/sync-changes`.

UNPLANNED CHECKPOINTS
Any non-bulk file-graph transact during a load writes everything pending, but at most one budget, so its stall is about the target:
- thread-api/transact from the UI
- the case-rename transact at reset.cljs:39
- a live watcher during re-index.

MEMORY
Dirty nodes and the tail stay pinned until a flush: dirty children are strong references (PSS 340-345, 383). bulk-max-datoms caps this.

OLD DB VALUES
The ADR-003 address-reuse hazard (a db value held across a flush reads rewritten leaves) is unchanged in kind. Its window is now per flush instead of per file.

CRASH CONSISTENCY (item 4)
- Each flush is one store-impl! → one -store → one SQLite `.transaction` (db_worker.cljs:152). It contains every dirty node, the root (addr 0) and an empty tail (addr 1) (storage.cljs:116-123).
- WAL with exclusive locking (db_worker.cljs:316-319).
- In-place upserts of reused addresses commit together with the new root. Split nodes get fresh addresses (storage.cljs:43-48).
- Each file is one DataScript tx, and flushes happen only between files. So the stored db is always the db as of the last flush: whole files only, never half a file. The same holds after an unplanned store-tail: root plus replayed tail is a consistent pair.
- Assumption, not verified: a committed transaction in the sqlite-wasm OPFS SAH pool survives a process kill.
- Lost work = files parsed since the last flush. Their markdown is intact.
- Next open (verified path):
  - restore-graph! → :graph/restored → :graph/ready → load-graph-files!.
  - The unparsed suffix and the lost pending files are "add" and are re-parsed. With this change, above 100 missing files they go through the bulk loader.
  - Unchanged gaps:

    - create-default-files! never ran, so a new graph may lack logseq/config.edn.
    - The Electron disk copy was exported at parse start (native_fs.cljs:140).
  - A persisted `:logseq.kv/bulk-load` {:status :in-progress | :done} marker would fix both of the first two. It works in file graphs, where gc already transacts `:logseq.kv/graph-last-gc-at`, db_worker.cljs:333-334. Write it in the first bulk tx (atomic with the first flush) and set it :done before the final flush. :graph/ready then resumes the bulk load and pubs :graph/added. Recommended follow-up.

- storage.cljs remember-db (85-89) keeps one WeakRef per store call in an unbounded vector. Fewer stores means fewer entries (minor).

| case | store per file | worker per file (≈ wall) | g-10k parse | vs today |

design.summary:
Proposal: index first-open content per file, and replace the full post-parse rebuild with a worker-side walk in small, resumable batches.

What the design does:

1. **Index every transaction, including first-open ones.** Drop the `:from-disk?` exclusion in `db_listener.cljs` and write the rows straight into the search db inside the transaction's own task. First open then fills `blocks_fts` file by file, entirely in the worker. The UI no longer has to trigger anything after parsing. This also fixes a second defect: watcher edits and reopen-reconcile edits are never indexed today.

2. **Manual rebuild and healing become a worker-owned walk.** New namespace `frontend.worker.search-indexer`:
   - It walks the AEVT `:block/uuid` index in entity-id order, with an integer cursor, from the current `@conn` on every slice. I chose AEVT over the AVET walk the task names: same entities, but entity-id order reads EAVT leaves in sequence instead of at random uuid positions.
   - Each slice has an 8 ms budget and always consumes at least one datom. The batch size adapts, and the time of the SQLite commit counts against the budget.
   - Rows and the cursor are committed in one SQLite transaction, so a quit resumes from the cursor.
   - Between slices it yields with `setTimeout`: 4 ms when the worker is idle, 40 ms if a thread-api call arrived in the last 300 ms.
   - A per-repo token stops the loop on close, truncate or a new rebuild.
   - The walk starts from the worker itself, on open, once no thread-api call has arrived for 1 s. No fixed 3 s delay and no UI turn is involved.

3. **Persisted state** lives in a new `search_meta (k, v)` table in the search db: `blocks_state` (`complete` or `building`), `blocks_cursor` (entity id) and `blocks_gen`. This answers the four required changes from the prior critique:
   - **Truncate vs new db:** the decision is made by the presence of the `blocks_state` row, not the `blocks` table. `truncate-table!` drops and recreates the tables and writes `building`/cursor 0/gen+1 in the same transaction. With no row, the state is `building` only for a file graph that already has `:file/path` datoms (a legacy or lost index); otherwise `complete` (a fresh graph, or any DB graph).
   - **Dedup:** there is no in-memory once-flag. New-graph transactions are indexed as they happen, so nothing needs marking stale. Re-index deletes the whole OPFS pool, search db included, so it starts fresh.
   - **Generations:** the walk never holds a db value or a lazy seq across a yield. Every transaction now reaches the incremental path, which upserts idempotently wherever the cursor is. The only bypass left in file graphs is a `:reset-conn!` report; it truncates, bumps the generation and restarts the walk.
   - **Budget accounting:** as in point 2.

4. **Fuse page index.** The rebuild no longer builds Fuse. At 10k it accounts for most of the measured 9 630 ms sync part, and with more than 2 500 pages `search-blocks` never uses Fuse anyway. The per-query count of every `:block/name` datom is capped at 2 501. The lazy Fuse build (at most 2 500 pages) can optionally run in slices through the same scheduler.

5. **Index state is shown.** The search palette (cmdk) shows "Block index building: N %" in the Nodes and current-page group headers. The manual-rebuild success notice appears only when the result is `complete`.

The fuller ADR-003 version is described where it differs: a rebuild without truncate using a `gen` column and swept deletes, index state carried on every search answer, an indexed-tx watermark, and coalesced first-open commits.

```clojure
(defn index-batch [db after-e {:keys [max-items max-chars deadline]}]

        (or (nil? dt) (not= :block/uuid (:a dt)))
        {:rows (persistent! rows) :last-e last-e :n n :done? true}
        (and (pos? n) (or (>= n max-items) (>= chars max-chars) (>= (js/performance.now) deadline)))
```

```clojure
(defn- run! [repo token]

    (swap! *jobs assoc-in [repo :running] token)
    (letfn [(finish [r] (swap! *jobs update repo dissoc :running) (log! repo r) (p/resolve! done r))
            (step [max-items]
```

- The search write moves from a promise-chained step to a synchronous call in the same task, inside `try/catch`. The worker does the same total work per keystroke, but a SQLite failure can no longer surface as an unhandled rejection.
- A `:reset-conn!` report (`db_worker.cljs:297`) no longer runs `sync-search-indice` over the whole old and new db. It truncates and restarts the walk instead.

**During a manual rebuild or a heal**

- Not surfaced in the smallest change: other `search-blocks` consumers can get partial answers while it builds:

design.summary:
On the journals home, every journal page on screen mounts its Linked References section. When a page has at least one reference, the section calls thread-api/get-view-data with :linked-references, which runs logseq.db.common.reference/get-linked-references. That function asks DataScript for "blocks that reference the page, or whose ancestor does" through the rules has-ref/parent (reference.cljs:110-115). DataScript runs the second has-ref branch as `(parent ?p ?b)` before the refs filter, with neither variable bound, so it reads every :block/parent datom in the graph — one per block — plus a join per nesting level. It then keeps only the blocks under a real reference. So the cost follows the number of blocks in the graph, and every :block/parent index leaf is read back from SQLite on the cold lazy db, whatever the page's reference count.

The "view with filters" row in step 1 (3.7-5.1 s) is the same call, labelled from truncated args: results.md:138 and :186 give the same 3701 ms number. The 2.2 s `q pull ?h` is a separate call. It is the built-in NOW query of the file-graph default config (state.cljs:381-389), rendered only on today's journal (page.cljs:714-715). Its first clause, `(task ?h ...)`, walks every task-marked block in the graph.

Smallest fix (step A): compute the same set without Datalog rules. Take the direct refs from the AVET index (ref attributes are always AVET-indexed), then walk their subtrees through :block/_parent, carrying include/exclude hits down each path. Also replace the alias rule, whose fourth branch reads every :block/alias datom, with entity navigation. The output is identical and the cost becomes O(refs + their subtrees). Tests: differential tests against the current Datalog version, and a test that counts SQLite restores to guard size-independence.

Fuller ADR-003 version (step B): a bounded batch endpoint. It walks the AVET slice (:block/refs, target, e) with a full-key cursor [target-idx e]. Budgets per batch: result limit, datoms scanned, and time. Every response carries a worker generation (a session nonce plus a counter bumped by a raw tx listener); a continuation from an older generation is rejected and restarted, never concatenated. The UI accumulates rows of one generation and groups them with a shared pure function. Batches come in entity-id order, an explicit behaviour change. It applies only to pages above a reference threshold; smaller pages keep the exact, correctly ordered step-A answer. An ordering index is the optional step C.

```clojure
        filter? (seq interesting)
        own-hits (fn [e] (if filter? (into #{} (keep #(interesting (:db/id %))) (:block/refs e)) #{}))
        ok? (fn [e hits] (and (every? hits includes)
                              (not-any? hits excludes)
                              (not-any? #(class-ids (:db/id %)) (:block/tags e))))
        seen (volatile! #{})
        out (volatile! (transient #{}))]
    (doseq [rid full-ref-block-ids
            :let [root (d/entity db rid)]
            :when (and root (not (@seen rid)))]
      (loop [stack (list [root (into (if filter? (ancestor-hits root interesting) #{}) (own-hits root))])]
        (when-some [[e hits] (first stack)]
          (let [eid (:db/id e)]
            (if (@seen eid)
              (recur (rest stack))
              (do (vswap! seen conj eid)
                  (when (ok? e hits) (vswap! out conj! eid))
                  (recur (into (rest stack)
                               (map (fn [c] [c (into hits (own-hits c))]))
                               (:block/_parent e)))))))))
    (persistent! @out)))
```

- The hits of a node = refs on its whole ancestor chain (roots seed theirs with ancestor-hits) plus its own refs.
- `seen` is safe: a nested direct ref reached through another root carries the same full-chain hits.

design.summary:
get-initial-data scales with the graph for two reasons. It ships the full EAVT of every page, and the full EAVT of every file, `:file/content` included. It also sets a UI contract: several UI paths quietly rely on the UI DataScript copy holding every page and every file's text. The most dangerous one is typing: the parser resolves `[[Page]]` against the UI db.

The plan has three phases. Each phase lands safely on its own.

**Phase 1 (size M): take file content out of the UI entirely.** Pages and page identity are unchanged.
- initial data ships only the `:file/path` datoms, read from AVET, with no per-file EAVT lookup; full EAVT is kept only for config.edn, custom.css and custom.js.
- recent-updated-pages is dropped for file graphs; nothing in a file graph uses it.

- This is the step that removes the size dependence (target under 100 ms and under 200 restores at any size).

**The fuller ADR-003 version** ships no pages at all. A worker boot endpoint returns materialized sidebar and home data with a db generation and freshness. The UI db is a pure cache, and every existence check goes through the worker.

design.ui_contract_risks:
**Phase 1: the UI db no longer holds file text, except for boot files.**
- Safe consumers, verified:
  - config.edn and custom.css at first paint; both stay in initial data.
  - Path-only lookups (file-exists?, get-file-page, get-file-page-id, delete-pages-by-files), because path datoms stay.
  - `<get-files` and `<get-file-paths`, which are worker-backed.
- Converted: the save path (P1.5-P1.7), code editor, raw file view, AST dev view, Refresh, and the sync code (P1.8, P1.9).
- Residual race: old content is still taken per write and set asynchronously. With FIFO worker→UI messages, write #2 can still carry content #1 while the disk holds #2's predecessor. That is the same as today, not a regression. The `logseq/bak` count check measures it.
- alter-file now captures the old content BEFORE the update. Today it probably reads after, when the UI mirror already holds the new text, so the change compares disk against what the app last knew. That is the intended semantics, but backups may appear in cases where none appeared before; the bak check covers it.
- A missed caller of alter-files still works: it fetches from the worker.
- A missed reader of `db/get-file` gets nil for non-boot files. The phase-3 lint guard also covers the `db/get-file` pattern.
- DB-graph paths are unchanged.

**Phase 2: no visible change while the UI db is complete** (the resolver is idempotent then), with two exceptions:
- `(and X [[missing]])` now returns nothing instead of X.
- `((uuid))` refs to blocks not loaded in the UI are kept instead of dropped. That fixes a probable pre-existing lazy-block bug; confirm with the test.

Other phase-2 risks:
- The stub rule rewrites only ref-position maps and top-level maps whose uuid is absent. Worker-internal rename and parse transacts do not pass through apply-ops! or thread-api/transact, so they are untouched.
- The DB-graph branch is unchanged (a `(not db-based?)` guard).

**Phase 3: the UI db becomes a lazy cache for pages.**
- Every class-A site degrades silently until it is converted: wrong or missing results, with no error. That is why the lint guard and allowlist land in the same change.
- Sites that already fall back to the worker cost one worker call per distinct unloaded page on screen: page-cp-inner, page-aux, `<get-block`, the journals list through get-view-data plus journal-cp. That cost is not graph-proportional.
- Pipeline tx-data applied by eid can create partial entities. Name lookups ignore entities without `:block/name`, `db/page?` filters them, and the page-cp change handles id lookups.
- Recent page ids from a different db (a re-index) are skipped when they have no `:block/name`.
- Mobile and desktop parity: everything stays in the worker.
- The `:file-graph-import?` full-datom path (db_worker.cljs:643-645) is unchanged.
design.expected_gain:
Baseline, g-10k reopen: get-initial-data sync 8689 ms, total 10 096 ms, 93 026 datoms, 18 358 restores (5.6 s restoring). g-real: 1436 ms, 7634 datoms, 1239 restores.

**Phase 1:**
- Content: the ~41 MB of `:file/content` (≈ the on-disk graph) leaves:
  - the transit write, which happens after the sync timer. It is most of the 1.4 s gap between total-ms and sync-ms.
  - the structured clone;
  - `d/conn-from-datoms` on the UI thread. Hypothesis: part of the 1834 ms UI task after the db opens.
  - the renderer heap. The file-content share of the 949 MB renderer is unmeasured.
- It also no longer comes back through load-graph-files!. P1.4 removes 10k UI transacts of file maps, which probably fill the 34-49 s activity windows; P1.0 confirms.
- Datoms: about −10k `:file/content`, and the per-file mtime, size and created-at datoms go too.
- Restores: the per-file EAVT lookups become one AVET walk. Whether that saves close to 0 or up to about half of the 18.4k restores depends on EAVT locality, since a file entity is allocated in the same tx as its page. P1.0 measures it.
- Honest estimate: get-initial-data falls to somewhere between about 4.5 s and 7.5 s at 10k. It stays linear in pages (~70k datoms).

**Phase 2:** no performance change. Per save it adds O(refs in the block) AVET lookups.

**Phase 3:**
- The boot set is constant-bounded: 3 files, at most 11 journals, contents, card, home, at most 100 favorites, at most 20 recent. That is a few hundred to about 1.5k datoms and at most about 150 EAVT restores.
- Expected under 100 ms at any size, and g-real and g-10k should converge. This is an estimate; check it against the perf-part records.

**What stays linear (separate items):**
- load-graph-files!: one disk read plus one worker call per file at every reopen. Next step: an mtime+size reconcile in the worker, resumable (ADR-003 plan step 2).
- get-view-data `:linked-references` (6.0 s) and the `?h` query (2.2 s).
- First open (~117 ms per file) and the FTS rebuild.
- User-initiated Refresh and re-index.
- In phase 3, async page loads scale with what is on screen, not with the graph.

**Acceptance metric:** time-to-journals-visible and the worker stalls in the first 60 s after reopen, not only get-initial-data sync-ms.
